title: Storage, spills and disposal
audience: Trainee or new worker on the window cleaning (all heights) track, working under supervision.
learningOutcomes: Explain and apply: storage, spills and disposal

instruction.heading: Exterior, height and access context
instruction.body: This lesson is part of the window cleaning (all heights) track. The track covers ground-level, water-fed pole and elevated access work on glazing and frames. Any work above ground level, or from a ladder, scaffold or elevating work platform, is restricted: it needs employer authorisation under a site-specific risk assessment, and the worker must hold any licence the relevant state or territory requires for the equipment used. This lesson does not grant the right to work at height or on solar systems.

instruction.heading: Instruction
instruction.body:
Learning goal and job context: This lesson teaches storage, spills and disposal for routine cleaning work. Start with the actual job scope, site instructions, manufacturer directions and worker training. Never treat a general lesson as authority to perform restricted or specialist work.

Core procedure: Store products upright, secured and in original or approved labelled containers, separated according to compatibility instructions. Check transport restraints and heat exposure. For a spill, first identify the substance and extent; do not enter an unknown atmosphere or improvise absorbents. Follow the SDS and site spill plan; escalate beyond training and equipment.

Decision-making in the field: Before acting, ask: What is the surface or equipment? What is the soil or hazard? Which product or method is approved? What could harm a person, property or food? If the answer is unclear, pause, protect the area and seek supervisor guidance.

Worked workplace scenario: An unlabelled bottle leaks in a van. The worker keeps people clear, reports it and does not pour the liquid down a drain.

Guided supervised practice: Inspect a mock chemical cupboard and transport crate; correct six staged faults and document an unknown-spill escalation.

Evidence and feedback: The assessor observes the task and checks whether the learner: recognises segregation, secondary containment and limits of personal spill-response authority. A learner must explain any unsafe choice, correct it and repeat the demonstration. Record observations, required coaching and reassessment rather than awarding competence from attendance alone.

instruction.heading: Stop-work rule
instruction.body: Stop-work rule: stop immediately, make the area safe, and tell your supervisor before resuming if the surface, anchor, ladder, platform or roof is unstable or uncertain; wind, rain, ice or fading light changes conditions; you see or suspect exposed wiring, damaged cable, water near electrical equipment or live parts; a person or animal enters the exclusion zone; the task falls outside your training, authorisation or the work order; or you are asked to work above ground level without the licence or authorisation required.

procedure: Store products upright and secured, in original or approved labelled containers, separated according to their compatibility instructions.
Check transport restraints and heat exposure before moving any product.
Follow the SDS and the site spill plan for the product involved.
For a spill, identify the substance and its extent before doing anything else.
Keep people clear, and do not enter an atmosphere you cannot identify.
Do not improvise absorbents, and do not pour liquid down a drain.
Report the spill, and escalate anything beyond your training and equipment to the supervisor.
Record the spill, the escalation and who was told.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Licence and height notice: This lesson does not grant the right to work at height, on roofs, from elevated work platforms, or on solar systems. Completing it is not a licence, certificate or authority for regulated work. Boom-type elevating work platforms need a high risk work licence in Victoria at any boom length, and in New South Wales, Queensland, Tasmania, the Northern Territory and Western Australia where the boom is 11 metres or more. The WorkSafe WA page (last updated 13 August 2026) and the NT WorkSafe bulletin (no date shown) both state the 11-metre threshold. Check whether this work needs a high-risk work licence with the state regulator before you start. Queensland's definition does not cover platforms under 11 metres (WorkSafe Queensland page, no date shown). Tasmania's WP licence applies where the boom length is 11 metres or more, and no licence is needed for a boom under 11 metres (WorkSafe Tasmania page, last updated 1 December 2023). In New South Wales and Queensland the boom length is 11 metres: a boom-type platform of 11 metres or more needs the licence, and a shorter boom may not need it in those states. Victoria's WP class has no boom-length threshold, so the licence is not limited by length there. This lesson does not grant a licence. Scissor lifts need no high risk work licence in Victoria or the Northern Territory. Check the licence rules for your state or territory and obtain your employer's written authorisation before any work above ground level.

Stop-work rule: stop immediately, make the area safe, and tell your supervisor before resuming if the surface, anchor, ladder, platform or roof is unstable or uncertain; wind, rain, ice or fading light changes conditions; you see or suspect exposed wiring, damaged cable, water near electrical equipment or live parts; a person or animal enters the exclusion zone; the task falls outside your training, authorisation or the work order; or you are asked to work above ground level without the licence or authorisation required.

qualityStandard: Products are stored upright, secured, labelled and separated by compatibility.
Transport restraints and heat exposure are checked before a product is moved.
The substance and extent of a spill are identified before any response, and unknown atmospheres are not entered.
Spill response follows the SDS and site spill plan, and liquids are not poured down a drain.
summary: Products are stored upright, secured and in original or approved labelled containers, separated according to their compatibility instructions.
For a spill, the substance and its extent are identified first, and no unknown atmosphere is entered and no absorbents are improvised.
The SDS and the site spill plan are followed, and anything beyond training or equipment is escalated.

knowledgeChecks.question: What should you check before performing storage, spills and disposal?
options: That products are stacked high to save space in the store, the van, the depot, the cart, the shed and the bin
That heavy bottles sit on the top shelf to keep the floor clear of the cart, the van, the bin and the store
That products are upright, secured, labelled and separated by compatibility, with transport restraints checked
That the van heater is on so the products stay warm for work, the cart, the depot, the store and the bin

knowledgeChecks.question: What do you do when a chemical spill occurs in storage?
options: Pour it down the drain so it is gone for good today, the room, the sink and the floor
Mop it up with a towel from the nearest cleaning cart at once in the store room
Keep people clear, follow the SDS and site spill plan, and escalate beyond your training
Enter the area quickly to see how big the spill is first, the leak and the fumes

knowledgeChecks.question: How does the lesson say products must be stored?
options: Upright, secured, in original or approved labelled containers, and separated by compatibility
Loose in the van so they can be reached quickly
On the top shelf regardless of weight
